note: kbc-cmd/1 — the ONE declaration home for kb-code's keyboard and command surface (v7 §P2). A binding that is not in this file does not exist: the `?` sheet, the command palette, the which-key overlay and the printable cheatsheet are all GENERATED from these rows, and `kb-code commands doctor` is the CI gate. Presets are three explicit COLUMNS, never inheritance — an empty array means 'unbound in that preset, reachable from the palette'.

presets.title: vim
presets.note: The shipped keymap: modal motions in the buffer, `g`/`z`/`[`/`]`/`m`/`'` prefixes, Space as the ONLY leader.

presets.title: plain
presets.note: No bare letters: arrows, F-keys and modifier chords in the VS Code idiom. A command with an empty column is palette-only, never silently inherited from vim.

presets.title: helix-ish
presets.note: vim plus helix's selection-first goto family (`ge`, `gs`, `ga`, `gn`/`gp`). Helix's `gh`/`gl` line motions are deliberately NOT adopted — `gh` is line history here.

reserved_chords.note: Chords the browser owns, written in the CANONICAL TOKEN FORM the dispatcher produces: modifiers in the fixed order Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Meta, and a SHIFTED PRINTABLE folded into the character (`Ctrl-T` is Ctrl+Shift+t; `Shift-` survives only on named keys like `Shift-Enter`, which have no shifted character to fold into). `hard` can never be claimed by any entry — `kb-code commands doctor` fails the build. `passthrough` may be claimed only by an entry that declares `browser_passthrough: true` (it WANTS the browser behaviour) or acknowledges the risk in `browser_reserved`. `Ctrl-w` is on the hard list and is nonetheless claimed as a PREFIX by the reader's pane chords, which is why those rows carry a `browser_reserved` acknowledgement naming the caveat the old cheat sheet omitted.

context_keys.note: which board surface is mounted. V74-L2 added `boards` — the kbc-canvas/1 board (`~boards/{slug}`), which is a DIFFERENT surface from `canvas` (V3.4-C2's frozen working-set canvas) and gates its own rows so the two sets are provably disjoint. V74-L3b added `tours` — the kbc-tour/1 playback (`~tours/{slug}`), which shares the WALKTHROUGH rows with `boards` (a tour IS a board whose nodes are its steps, server invariant 26(a)) and gates nothing else on this key.
a tour / resize submode / canvas selection is active
an inline peek (a CM6 block widget under the caret line) is open in the focused pane (V70-A6)
this tab was opened trail-linked (`?trail=&step=`) and knows its origin (V70-A6)
a Ramp-participating result list has a focused row (V70-A6)
the focused pane is provisional (peek→pane promotion, not yet pinned) (V70-A6)

which CENTER mode the shell has mounted (`web-code/src/desk/centerModes.ts`'s SHIPPED_CENTER_MODES). V72-G1.2 added `dossier` (`?ent=`); the dossier's own keys gate on it so they are inert everywhere else.

V74-L2 — a kbc-canvas/1 board is running its walkthrough (`?step=`). It splits the board's own key set in two PROVABLY DISJOINT halves (`!walkthrough` vs `walkthrough`), which is what lets `k` mean "previous card" while reading and "previous step" while walking without either row shadowing the other.

conflict_policy: A CONFLICT is one key sequence bound to two different commands in two COACTIVE scopes at the SAME modal depth (or in one scope under `when` predicates that are not provably disjoint). Those rows must appear in both entries' `ratified_conflicts` or `kb-code commands doctor` fails. A key bound in a DEEPER scope shadows the shallower one by design (that is what a modal stack is) and is reported as `shadowed`, not gated. A `scope: global` key re-declared in a narrower scope is the internal SHADOWING LINT, with three structural exemptions: `Escape` (the dismiss stack is a scope ladder, gated instead on a distinct `dismiss_order`), a row carrying a `vim_kind` (its executor is the CM6 layer, which stops the event at `Prec.highest` before the window host sees it — `:` is the live case, go-to-line in the buffer and the palette everywhere else), and an explicitly ratified pair. The ratification list is a SNAPSHOT of decisions taken when it was written, never a computed identity: a collision introduced later will not be in it, and the gate stays red until a human moves the key or writes down why it stays.

commands.title: Back up the reading flow
commands.note: Replaces the review diff's and the tour's old Esc-navigates behaviour (Esc only dismisses). V70-A6: in a TRAIL-LINKED tab (`?trail=&step=`) whose origin is not already behind us in this tab's history, `u` PUSHES the origin instead — the destination stays exactly one Back away — and it never tries to focus another tab. Everywhere else it is still plain browser Back; there is no second stack. `vim_kind` exists because `u` is a BARE key: `CommandRoot`'s guard 2 gives the buffer every bare key, and A3's "focus follows the file" lands DOM focus there the instant a trail-linked tab's destination renders — exactly when this needs to fire. `vimReader.ts`'s `cb-nav-back` arm forwards to this SAME handler by id (`bus.run`), never a second copy of the trail-origin decision.

Bare `i` is safe from inside the read-only CodeView: the vim reducer reacts to `i` only under the `g` prefix (`gi`, the impact panel), so `i` carries no `vim_kind`, `shouldWithholdFromBuffer` resolves it exactly and lets it through, and nothing fires twice.

An explicit keystroke is the only thing allowed to move the reader onto a likely/candidate target — D5's rule bans AUTO-navigation, not a deliberate one — and with several atoms on the line the command takes the first and says so rather than guessing. `Space l` ("link") rather than the `Space o` this row first claimed: V73-K2b landed `doc.card-open` on `Space o` in `review` scope, and a GLOBAL row owning that key would fail the shadowing lint on THEIR row, not this one. Note the conflict pass cannot see a global/global collision at all (it skips any pair where either scope is `global`), so a leader letter must be checked against the whole registry by hand before it is claimed.
